amendments.rule: Rules 53, 62, 63 and 68 decide a verbless clause's supplied copula and subject by what is left in the clause to carry them, and none of them says what happens when a **modifier** stands inside the predicate phrase. It is not the carrier. A **determiner-carrying article** keeps only its own English determiner under rule 21, and the **predicate noun** takes the supplied words, discontinuously under rule 15. `οὕτως καὶ τῆς παρακλήσεως` → *so are ye also of the comfort* gives *of the* to the article and the discontinuous *are ye … comfort* to `παρακλήσεως`, as the same verse's `τῶν παθημάτων` → *of the sufferings* gives *of the* to its article and *sufferings* to its noun — one construction, one analysis, which is rule 24. The corpus is what settles this: no unit anywhere aligns an article to an English supplied **subject pronoun** it does not itself realize, while nine put a supplied subject and copula together on a predicate noun — `κοινωνός` → *he is partner*, `ἀπόστολοι` → *they are the messengers* and `δόξα` → *they are the glory* at 2CO.8.23, `θεός` → *it is God* at 2CO.4.6, `κτίσις` → *he is a creature*, `ὥρᾳ` → *it was at hour*, `λόγια` → *it were oracles*. 2CO.5.13's `θεῷ` → *it is unto God* is the shape to hold in mind: there the noun takes the case preposition as well, and its note records that it does so only because no article stood to anchor it — so where one does stand, rule 21 gives the article that preposition and nothing more. An **attributive quantifier or numeral** standing in that phrase is no more the carrier than an article is, and the expletive *there* of an English existential is a supplied subject like any other, decided the same way. `εἷς θεός` → *there is one God* gives a bare *one* to the numeral and the discontinuous *there is … God* to `θεός`, as `οὐδεὶς θεός` → *there is no God* gives a bare *no* to the quantifier and *there is … God* to `θεός`, and as 1TI.2.5 reads the identical frame. A **negative** quantifier is not the exception: rules 41, 59 and 87 decide where the English negation goes and say nothing about a supplied verb, so carrying the clause's negation does not make a quantifier the carrier of one. Where the negative word is itself the **predicate** rather than a modifier of one, rule 63 applies in the ordinary way and the copula is its helper, `οὐδὲν εἴδωλον ἐν κόσμῳ` → *no idol is anything in the world* keeping *is* on `οὐδέν`; so the test is the one rule 63 already states, which nominal the clause predicates of the other, and never which of them is negative or which stands first. Rules 22, 31, 32, 89 and 90 are untouched and are the contrast: an article that itself realizes a pronoun, a relativizer or an address word may of course carry a copula predicated of it, which is why `τοὺς ἐν πάσῃ θλίψει` → *them that are in any affliction* is unaffected. Rule 62's preposition carrier is not a model for an article, rule 67 having already warned that such an analogy jumps carrier classes.
amendments.why: 1CO.8 wrote the same existential frame twice — εἷς θεός at 8:6 and οὐδεὶς θεός at 8:4 — and the two verses placed the supplied 'there is' on different tokens, because rule 96 named only an article as the modifier that is not the carrier and left a quantifier or numeral unaddressed. The amendment widens the rule's own holding to any modifier inside the predicate phrase, keeping every existing sentence intact, and adds the negative-quantifier guard (rules 41, 59 and 87 govern the English negation, not a supplied verb) together with the rule 63 contrast that keeps 8:4's first clause right. Returned as an amendment rather than a new rule because the over-broad reading is rule 96's opening sentence itself, which a later pass would read first; 1TI.2.5 (θεός → 'there is god', head 'god') is the corpus precedent and no shown corpus row places a supplied existential on a quantifier.

conventions: εἰδωλόθυτον is analysed by whether an article governs it, not by the English phrasing. Where one does (8:1, 8:4, 8:10) the article takes the supplied nominal things — with any case preposition riding along, as of things at 8:4 — and the adjective takes sacrificed to idols headed on sacrificed (rules 22, 102). Where the Greek is anarthrous (8:7) no article competes and the whole supplied expression a thing sacrificed to an idol belongs to the adjective, its determiners being rule 51 helpers and thing the generic completion, headed on the same word (rule 17).

A supplied English existential there is rides with the predicate noun of a verbless clause and never with an attributive quantifier or numeral standing in front of it: εἷς θεός → there is one God (8:6) and οὐδεὶς θεός → there is no God (8:4) both give the discontinuous there is … God to θεός and leave the quantifier its own bare word. A negative quantifier is not an exception; carrying the clause's negation does not make it the carrier of a supplied verb. Where the negative is itself the predicate, as οὐδέν is in 8:4's first clause, rule 63 governs instead and the copula is its helper.

report: One real cross-verse split: the supplied existential 'there is' over [quantifier + θεός]. At 8:6 εἷς θεός → 'there is one God' puts 'there is … God' on θεός (rule 68) and leaves εἷς a bare 'one'; at 8:4 οὐδεὶς θεός → 'there is no God' put 'there is no' on οὐδείς and left θεός a bare 'God'. Same frame, and nothing in the source licenses the difference — a quantifier's negativity does not move a supplied verb. 8:4 is patched to match 8:6 and the corpus (1TI.2.5, θεός → 'there is god', head 'god').

8:4's first clause is deliberately left alone and is not part of that split: in οὐδὲν εἴδωλον ἐν κόσμῳ the negative is the clause's own predicate, so rule 63 keeps 'is' on οὐδέν, whereas in οὐδεὶς θεός it is attributive and the noun is the only nominal the existential can predicate of. The verse's earlier 'one analysis for the verse' note rested on a false parallel between the two clauses; the patch's review notes now record why the Greek differs.

Checked and found licensed rather than split: εἰδωλόθυτον ×4 — 8:1, 8:4 and 8:10 have an article that takes the supplied nominal 'things' (rules 22, 102), while 8:7 is anarthrous and the whole 'a thing sacrificed to an idol' is the adjective's (rules 51, 17), the head staying on 'sacrificed' every time. The same test accounts for πᾶς ('all men' on the anarthrous quantifier at 8:7, 'things' on the article at 8:6). τις → 'any man' head 'any' at 8:2 and 8:3 against 'a man' head 'man' at 8:10 follows the ASV's own wording, and both heads are corpus-majority (48 and 20 units). ἀσθεν-: the copula participle takes the supplied copula and the adjective takes 'weak' at 8:7 and 8:10, while the finite-recast participle carries the whole frame at 8:11 and 8:12. Every article treatment (unrepresented at 8:1, 8:3, 8:8, 8:13; 'that' at 8:7 under rule 60; 'who' at 8:10 under rule 90 against 'he' + 'that is weak' at 8:11 under rule 32) turns on what the ASV wrote.

The chapter has no added units, so the table's blindness to them was checked against the dump directly: both italicized words — 'anything' at 8:4 and 'of' at 8:7 — are folded onto a licensing token, and neither verse marks a supplied word added while the other folds it. No fold/add split.

8:8 reviewed and left as it stands. The projection carries r00-base over s009–s017, which v009's evidence excluded, and the ASV follows the reversed clause order; every projection token still has an English counterpart, so this is rule 15 reordering and not rule 97. γάρ is unrepresented on the English alone, and the two οὔτε are aligned positionally to the fixed English 'neither … nor' rather than to the clauses they introduce in the projection, which would cross the pair. Both choices carry notes on the verse.

BSB: none of the four disagreements is an error, and each is the documented convention difference the contract names. 8:5 καί 'Even' — the ASV writes only 'For though' and rule 65 decides an intensifying καί on the English alone. 8:7 τῇ — the dative of custom is recast as 'being used' with no determiner (rule 23). 8:8 τῷ 'to' — rule 21 names τῷ θεῷ → 'to God' as one unit on the noun and forbids a bare 'to' on the article. 8:13 τόν — 'for evermore' gives the article nothing (rules 23, 30). No accepted edge was changed to improve the rate.
Two conventions recorded and one amendment returned, to rule 96, widening its modifier-is-not-the-carrier holding from an article to an attributive quantifier or numeral.
